en: Thus, in this book, there are two hundred and sixty-two sections, adorned with twenty-two chapters within six divisions.
The Milinda-pañhā that have been transmitted are complete; those yet to come number forty-two.
When all those that have been transmitted and those yet to come are combined, there are three hundred and four questions in total, all of which are designated by the name "Milinda-pañhā.
At the conclusion of the King’s and the Elder’s questions and answers, [the earth] extending to the edge of the waters was eight million four hundred thousand yojanas in thickness.
When he had spoken thus, this great earth shook in six ways, streaks of lightning flashed forth,
the deities rained down a shower of celestial flowers, Great Brahmā gave his approval, and a great roar arose like the sound of thunder rumbling from within the belly of the great ocean;
then King Milinda and the company of women in the harem, bowing their heads with palms joined in reverence, paid him homage.
King Milinda, his heart exceedingly joyful, his pride thoroughly subdued, perceiving the essence in the Buddha’s teaching and becoming free from doubt,
devoid of guile, and humble toward the Triple Gem, was deeply inspired by the Elder’s virtues, his mode of life, and his deportment.
Trusting, detached, with the pillar of pride destroyed, like a lord of serpents with its fangs extracted, he spoke thus:
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! This question concerning the domain of the Buddha has been answered by you.
In this teaching of the Buddha, there is no one equal to you in answering questions, except for the Elder Sāriputta, the General of the Dhamma.
Venerable Nāgasena, forgive my transgression; may you accept me as a lay follower, venerable Nāgasena.”
“From this day forth, for as long as life shall last, I have gone for refuge.
Then the king, together with his army, having paid homage to the Elder Nāgasena, had a monastery named Milinda built and dedicated it to the Elder;
he served Nāgasena and the hundred million monks with the four requisites.

Furthermore, having gained confidence in the Elder’s wisdom, he handed over the kingdom to his son, went forth from the home life into homelessness, and by developing insight, attained arahantship. Thus it was said:
“Wisdom is praised in the world...”
Having established the true Dhamma and destroyed doubt with wisdom,
the wise attain peace.
In whatever aggregate wisdom is established,
there mindfulness is not lacking;
it is the support for the attainment of distinction.
It is the foremost, the best, the unsurpassed;
therefore, a wise person,
seeing their own welfare, [should practice it].
"One should honor one possessed of wisdom with reverence,
as if honoring a shrine.
In the city of Doṇa in Laṅkā,
Having been written by the Great Elder named Doṇināmi while he was dwelling there,
it has been well-established according to what was heard.
The Questions of King Milinda and the Answers of Nāgasena;
for Milinda was indeed possessed of great wisdom.
Nāgasena is truly wise.
By this meritorious deed,
from here I go to the Tusita heaven.
"In the future, may I behold Metteyya;
may I hear the supreme Dhamma.
Thus ends the *Milindapañha*.
